A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Tora and contain readable, matchable text, equations, figures and tables. The supplied v1 ends with references; v3 includes an appendix. All pages support comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original benchmark comparisons and ablations, alongside generated examples and resolution/duration analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds qualitative OpenSora comparisons, dataset analyses and a motion-VAE comparison in Table 7.

M1.justification: The described inference pipeline gains GPT-4o prompt refinement before generation, explained in Data Processing and the appendix. The TE/ST-DiT/MGF architecture, reconstruction objective and dense-to-sparse training remain unchanged; expanded VAE training documentation does not establish another architectural change.

E1.justification: The approximately 630k-video training collection, 185-clip benchmark and text/image/trajectory-controlled generation coverage are retained. The appendix identifies previously unspecified data sources and examines the existing motion-compression task; it does not establish an expanded population or distinct generation scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VideoComposer, DragNUWA, AnimateAnything, TrailBlazer and MotionCtrl. v3 additionally evaluates OpenSora qualitatively in Figure 7 and an unadapted Pure Video VAE against the motion VAE in Table 7.

E3.justification: The stated batch-size range changes from 1–25 to 1–50, and the flow-score filtering threshold changes from greater than 3 to greater than 2. Table 7 adds PSNR/SSIM reconstruction evaluation. Figure 9c lists 408-frame training buckets despite the retained main-text range of 51–204 frames. These reported differences do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a motion-VAE fine-tuning ablation in Table 7, OpenSora failure-case comparisons in Figure 7, and visual evidence for the existing compression alternatives in Figure 8. The original compression, fusion, placement, training-strategy and resolution/duration analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly reports means and standard deviations for dataset durations, frame counts and caption lengths. These describe corpus variability, not experimental uncertainty; neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. New Table 7 reports Pure Video VAE versus Our VAE values of 27.34 versus 28.76 PSNR, 0.842 versus 0.860 SSIM, and 17.09 versus 14.25 TrajError. Figures 7–8 add qualitative findings, while Tables 5–6 add dataset statistics. These are additional results, not improvements between versions under a matched setting.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical substance are retained. Changing the motion-feature dimension notation from dv to d′ is equivalent notation; no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first trajectory-oriented DiT integrating text, images and trajectories, scalable generation up to 204 frames at 720p, and improved physical realism. Rewriting the abstract and contributions does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: The appendix adds explanations linking trajectory constraints to improved object stability relative to OpenSora, motivating motion-VAE adaptation through video/flow domain differences, and describing pooling failures on complex turns. The cycling and lantern interpretations are retained through relocation.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information: motion-VAE data sources, freezing, 384M parameters and 200,000 training iterations; filtering thresholds and preprocessing tools; bucket assignments; evaluation-source datasets and mask-center trajectories; and the GPT-4o refinement instructions. Conversely, v1’s explicit PLLaVA-13B captioner specification disappears.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for optical-flow and segmentation datasets and the GPT-4 report, while removing Lumiere and Tune-A-Video. MotionCtrl’s duplicate preprint/publication entries are consolidated. The central positioning relative to U-Net methods and DiT research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the introduction, methodological explanations and experimental discussion are rewritten or condensed. Data processing moves before training strategy, qualitative discussion moves into a structured appendix, and author/affiliation information changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 7–10 and Tables 5–7, revises architecture diagrams and Figure 5’s colors, grid and axis extent, and reformats and relocates existing tables. Figure 2 drops the cycling row, whose example remains in Figure 6. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1’s underdocumented benchmark construction and critical motion-VAE training, improving experimental auditability and reproducibility. Table 7 and Figure 7 also provide useful evidence for motion-specific adaptation and comparison with the backbone. The 408-versus-204-frame inconsistency and still-unreported human evaluation remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
